body.text: There are four practical ways to sell old silk sarees in India: consignment through a curated store, resale marketplaces, buying and selling groups on social media, and local old saree buyers who pay by weight for the silver in the zari. They pay very differently, and the right one depends almost entirely on what you have.
If your saree is handwoven silk with real zari, selling it by weight is almost always the worst outcome available to you.
What should you check before selling an old silk saree?
Before approaching anyone, spend twenty minutes on this. It changes what you should do next.

**Is the fibre silk?** Tilt it under a light and watch for a sheen that shifts colour. Rub a section between your palms and feel whether it warms. Our guide on [how to identify a pure silk saree](/journal/how-to-identify-pure-silk-saree) covers every test.

**Is the zari real?** Find a loose end at the very edge and scrape the metal gently. Pure zari stays silver right through. A reddish copper colour underneath means tested zari, which is worth much less. A thin film with no metal at all means metallic zari.
**What is the condition?** Look hard at the fold lines, the pallu and the borders. Note anything honestly, including stains and thin patches. Hiding them only produces a dispute later.
**What do you know about it?** Where it was bought, roughly when, who wore it and for what. This is provenance, and it genuinely affects value.

images.alt: Checking the fold lines of an old silk saree before selling it

body.text: What are the four ways to sell an old saree?

**Consignment with a curated store.** You send the saree, and the store authenticates, photographs, describes and lists it. You receive a share when it sells. It usually brings the best price for a good saree, and you do none of the work. In exchange you wait for a buyer, and not every saree will be accepted.
Best for handwoven silk, real zari, designer pieces and anything with a history.

**General resale marketplaces.** You list, photograph, price, answer questions and post the saree yourself. You keep full control and pay no commission, but it takes a great deal of your time, and buyers often expect to negotiate.
Best for volume, or for pieces whose market you already know.

**Buying and selling groups on social media.** Groups on Facebook and Instagram, often with an established set of members. Prices tend to sit between the two above. The catch is trust, because payment and postage rest entirely on you and the buyer.
Best if you already belong to one of these communities.

**Selling to old saree buyers by weight.** Many local old saree buyers pay by weight for the silver in real zari. It is fast and certain, but it pays a fraction of what the saree is worth as a saree, and the piece is destroyed in the process.
Reasonable only for sarees too damaged to wear.
What affects the price of an old silk saree?
In rough order of importance:

items: **Fibre.** Pure silk and everything else are separate markets.
**Zari.** Real metal changes the number substantially.
**Condition,** particularly the state of the fold lines.
**Weave and origin.** A documented Kanjeevaram or Banarasi carries more than an unidentified silk.
**Provenance.** A saree with a known story sells faster and for more.
**Colour and design.** Some periods and palettes are simply more wanted.

body.text: What mistakes should you avoid when selling a saree?
**Cleaning it aggressively first.** Well meant and frequently damaging. A professional dry clean is fine. Home washing is not.
**Hiding the flaws.** Photograph them clearly. Buyers who know what they are getting rarely send things back.

**Accepting the first offer on something you have not identified.** If you are unsure whether the zari is real, find out before you sell. It can be the difference between a few hundred rupees and a few thousand.
Which old sarees are worth the most?

Handwoven Kanjeevaram, Banarasi and other traditional weaves. Anything with pure zari. Sarees from the 1960s to the 1980s, whose colours and borders are no longer produced. Named designer pieces. And anything that comes with a story you can tell.
A saree that has been kept well is worth more again. Our guide on [how to care for silk sarees](/journal/how-to-care-for-silk-sarees) explains what well kept looks like.

items.question: Where can I sell old silk sarees in India?
items.answer: Through consignment with a curated store, on resale marketplaces, in buying and selling groups on social media, or to local old saree buyers who pay by weight. For good silk with real zari, consignment usually brings the best result.

items.question: How do I know if the zari in my saree is real?
items.answer: Scrape a loose end gently. Pure zari stays silver right through. Tested zari shows copper underneath. Metallic zari has no metal at all, only a shiny film.

items.question: Is it better to sell to an old saree buyer or on consignment?
items.answer: It depends on the saree. A badly damaged saree with real zari may be worth most by weight. A wearable silk saree in good condition is worth far more to someone who will wear it, which is what consignment is for.

items.question: Should I clean a saree before selling it?
items.answer: A professional dry clean is fine. Do not wash silk or zari at home, which can damage both and lower the price.

items.question: Which old sarees are worth the most?
items.answer: Handwoven Kanjeevaram and Banarasi sarees, anything with pure zari, pieces from the 1960s to the 1980s, named designer sarees, and sarees that come with a documented history.

items.question: Does From The Trunk take old sarees?
